target_name: Conservative Cushion per Dollar of Total Claims
rationale: Mechanically sound and sign-consistent, but it is a deflator/numerator recombination of two archive signals whose FMB slopes were both ~0.3, so the stated rationale that adding liabilities to the denominator will "lift the slope" is directly contradicted by the total-claims parent that already did exactly that and still produced a slope of 0.35.

Signs are internally consistent and the two legs do target economically distinct populations, but the construction re-uses the exact SUMRANK(cushion-to-price, quality leg) template already tested in "Two-Sided Cushion and Earnings Stability Score," so the marginal information is the growth-mismatch leg rather than the design.

target_name: Price Collapse With Intact Balance Sheet
rationale: The valuation leg is a coarse annual-price restatement of the well-documented nearness-to-52-week-high / long-term-reversal anomalies, and the proposal never acknowledges that the two published effects imply opposite signs at different horizons, leaving the expected sign asserted rather than argued.

This is the mirror of the previous proposal with the same known price-anomaly leg, and the MIN operator makes its low end a mixture of "near the high" and "low claim ratio" firms, so the spread does not isolate the claimed contrast and the "controlled experiment" interpretation does not hold.

target_name: Log Solvency Distance Including Market Value
rationale: Algebraically (act+mcap)/(lt+mcap) = 1 + (act−lt)/(lt+mcap), so the log is a strictly monotone transform of the archive's "Liquid Cushion per Dollar of Total Claims" and will reproduce its rank-sorted portfolio results exactly, making the "genuinely different market-augmented solvency distance" claim false and the only possible change a mild FMB outlier effect.

This is a pure operator swap (MIN to SUMRANK) on the identical two legs of an existing archive signal — the textbook cosmetic variant the objective warns against — and the proposal's own argument that it "keeps essentially the same firms at the top" concedes it will not deliver substantively new portfolio evidence.
